messages:
Samir Kapoor: Quick doc bug: API ref for DELETE /v1/resources/{id} shows a 200 response with a JSON body {"deleted": true}. The service actually returns 204 No Content on success. I opened a tiny PR to fix responses/examples and the SDK snippets. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/docs/pulls/4789
Elena Ruiz: Good catch. That mismatch causes client code to try parsing JSON and throw on 204. We should update the OpenAPI responses: 204 with no content, and keep a 404 example for not-found with body. Also update client snippets to not call res.json() for delete success.
Marco Li: Suggested change for snippets:

// JS
const res = await client.delete(`/v1/resources/${id}`)
if (res.status === 204) return { success: true }
const payload = await res.json() // for error responses


// curl
curl -X DELETE "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/resources/rsrc_123" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -i

Add note in API compatibility: older SDK helpers auto-parsed bodies and swallowed 204s; recommend checking status === 204.
Samir Kapoor: Also the HTML page had an example response block showing JSON; we need to remove that and add a short explanation block: "Successful delete returns 204 No Content. Error responses include JSON with error fields."
docs-bot: Automated check  PR 4789 created and passed lint: https://git.redwood/infra/docs/pulls/4789 :white_check_mark:
QA Bot: Quick test request added to PR checklist to verify 204 is rendered and SDK snippets updated (run preview): added as task #3.
Elena Ruiz: I'll update the OpenAPI YAML and the static example in the docs. Marco, can you patch the JS/Go snippets in the SDK examples?
Marco Li: Yep, I'll push a small patch for JS + Go and ensure both avoid res.json() on 204.
Samir Kapoor: Thanks all. Once merged, I'll ping support in case customers saw parse errors. Will mark resolved after merge. :white_check_mark:
